newsitem.title: ITALY: RUGBY UNION-ITALY BEGIN CAMPAIGN FOR FIVE NATIONS STATUS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ITALY BEGIN CAMPAIGN FOR FIVE NATIONS STATUS.

text.p: Italy will launch their campaign for a place in the Five Nations rugby union tournament when they take on Wales at Rome's Olympic stadium on Saturday.
The Welsh match kicks off a run of six internationals in three months in which the Italians hope to strengthen their case for a permanent place among the elite of European rugby.
The fixtures include meetings with all the Five Nations countries as well as an Australian side next month.
"Autumn presents a true test for a possible six nations tournament," said Giancarlo Dondi, president of the Italian Rugby Federation this week.

While Wales beat Italy at Cardiff last January, in recent seasons the Italians have offered convincing evidence that they have come of age a rugby playing nation, with wins over Scotland and Ireland as well as a narrow defeat to world champions South Africa.
Despite the fighting talk, the Italians still go into the match as clear underdogs. The domestic rugby season is just two weeks old and its players badly lack match practice.
"Wales will be much better prepared than us," said Italy's French coach Georges Coste, "But respect doesn't just come from winning but also fighting like lions against a team like Wales."
The first-ever full international between Italy and Wales on Italian soil will also see Gareth Llewellyn set rugby history by becoming the first Welsh forward to win 50 caps.
Llewellyn led Wales in the latter stages of last week's 40-33 defeat to France at Cardiff Arms Park, but hooker Jonathan Humphreys will return as skipper after recovering from a hamstring strain.
He will be joined by Cardiff team mates lock Derwyn Jones and flanker Hemi Taylor.
Jones, the 2.08-metre tall line-out ace, is recalled after the neck injury suffered by Mike Voyle while Taylor has recovered from shoulder damage to reclaim his blind-side flanker's role.
The Italians will be handicapped by the absence of prop forwards Missimo Giovannelli and Mark Giacheri, two of their most experienced players.
Giovannelli was unavailable for selection after failing to register with the Italian rugby federation for the current season, while Giacheri is still playing club rugby in Australia.
The Welsh match will be rugby's second apperance in the Olympic Stadium, Italy's soccer temple.

Italy (probable): 15-Massimo Ravazzolo; 14-Paolo Vaccari, 13-Stefano Bordon, 12-Ivan Francescato, 11-Leandro Manteri; 10-Diego Dominguez, 9-Alessandro Troncon; 8-Carlo Checchinato, 7-Orazio Arancio, 6-Andrea Sgorlon, 5-Diego Scaglia, 4-Pierpaolo Pedroni, 3-Franco Properzi Curti, 2-Carlo Orlandi, 1-Massimo Cuttitta (captain).

Wales: 15-Wayne Proctor; 14-Simon Hill, 13-Gareth Thomas, 12-Scott Gibbs, 11-Dafydd James; 10-Neil Jenkins, 9-Robert Howley; 8-Stephen Williams, 7-Kingsley Jones, 6-Hemi Taylor, 5-Derwyn Jones, 4-Gareth Llewellyn, 3-John Davies, 2-Jonathan Humphreys (captain), 1-Christian Loader.
